findings.detail: Commit e83f5c5 adopted `c.value == null` on the stated principle "reject what breaks, tolerate what the runtime already handles" — an explicit `null` is indistinguishable from absent at every consumer, so rejecting it discarded the user's whole template. The three sibling optional fields did not get the same treatment: `isMultiline`, `condition`, and `conditions` are all checked with `=== undefined`, so an explicit `null` on any of them fails `isFieldDef`, which fails `isFieldDefArray`, which throws away the entire saved template and resets to `INITIAL_FIELDS`. Every one of those nulls is already handled at runtime: `isFieldVisible` does `f.conditions || (f.condition ? [f.condition] : [])` (ProjectSummaryTab.tsx:244) — both nulls are falsy and fall through correctly — and `isMultiline` is only ever read for truthiness. This is the same over-rejection data-loss shape the PR just fixed, one field over. Severity is low rather than medium because no current write path produces those nulls: `addCondition` writes `{ fieldId: '', value: '' }` and `removeCondition` writes `[]`, never `null`. It would be medium if a hand-edited localStorage entry, an older build, or a future serializer that emits explicit nulls were in scope — the blast radius when it does trigger is total loss of the user's template, which is the failure mode the test file itself calls the more dangerous one.
findings.summary: `== null` tolerance applied to `value` but not to its sibling optional fields

findings.detail: Observation, not a request — the `else` branch and the surrounding `catch` predate this PR's base, so this is outside what the diff adds and I am not asking for it here. Noting it because the PR's own subject is exactly this recovery path: when `isFieldDefArray(parsed)` returns false, the user's customised template is replaced by `INITIAL_FIELDS` and the only signal is `console.error` in a devtools panel they will not have open. From the user's seat that is indistinguishable from "the app forgot my template." The PR correctly identifies over-rejection as the dangerous direction and has now narrowed it substantially, but the residual case is still silent, and the raw string is still sitting in `localStorage` unread at that moment.
findings.summary: Rejected template falls back to defaults with only a console message
